photos.c: Above: Reminding us of the "good old days" when middle-distance men also shone at cross-country, Matt Yates ran to 66th place in the National at Newark - and could no doubt have gone higher still.

Left: Getting ready for the "off" at Brockwell Park. Stuart Paton, Ted Pallant (President), Alex Luce, Rob Harding, Marlon Anderson (obscured), Steve Hewes, Said Chettati, Gerry Adams, Charlie Dickinson, Mike Nouch, Jim Estall, Derek Manning (behind), Tony Binda, Roger Alsop, Mick Graham (behind), Matt Yates, Alan Mead, Bruce Barton (behind), Bill Bull.

9.Matt Yates scored some great double wins over 800 and 1,500 metres. Pictured at Copthall where he had already taken the 'A' 800 event, he controls the 'B' 1,500m before sprinting away from the field.

Matt Yates (right) gave one of his best ever Games performances in Budapest, placing 6th in a highly tactical 1500 metres final. John Mayock (left) was 5th and Tony Whiteman (centre) was 4th. No medals but it was great to see all three Brits well in contention in a European Games final again.
